clue.text: Country dweller's security device protecting silver

indicators.note: one piece guards another by wrapping round it, so the silver sits inside the device

parts.note: a cotter is a pin or wedge that holds parts of a machine securely in place
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A villager's lock guarding the family silver.
explanation.walkthrough: A cotter is a fastening pin, a little-known security device; the 's after the definition is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager is someone living in a small house in a village or rural area.

clue.text: Gutless type whose encounter was briefly filmed

definitions.meaning: the playwright Noël of that surname wrote the play that became the film Brief Encounter

explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' hides the film title Brief Encounter (1945), scripted by Noël Coward from his own play.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutless type is a person without bravery, a classic synonym; the second sense names the dramatist Noël.

clue.text: Demon driver's overturning spoils fungus

parts.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is the archetypal reckless motorist

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for spoils is flipped over, read upwards

parts.note: loots means plunders or spoils

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist's crash wrecks a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' turns LOOTS into STOOL; the 's is 'has', a link. Mr Toad, from Kenneth Grahame's children's book, is famous for crashing motor cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a fungus, typically an inedible or poisonous mushroom.

clue.text: Simple though callous, as East Enders may put it

indicators.text: as East Enders may put it
indicators.note: London's East Enders, Cockneys, drop the h, so the word is pronounced in their accent

parts.note: callous means unfeeling, heartless

explanation.surface: Someone naive but also unkind, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys from London's East End drop initial H, so HEARTLESS comes out as 'artless.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means simple, natural and without guile.

clue.text: Standing up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone rising to their feet ahead of a court appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, standing straight up.

clue.text: One thus secure in the meteorologist's line

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means thus, in this way
to bar a door is to secure it

explanation.surface: A forecaster confined to one particular line on the chart.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map an isobar is a line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Leisurely stroll one's Aunt Ermintrude takes

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its run of letters, as if containing it

explanation.surface: An elderly aunt's daily constitutional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' signals a run of letters inside 'one's Aunt Ermintrude'.
explanation.definitionFit: To saunter is to walk in a slow, relaxed way; as a noun it is such a stroll.

clue.text: Dim bachelor beginning to learn organ

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A slow-witted single man starting organ lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear means dim or blurred, as of eyes or vision.

clue.text: Ringing old granny in lodging-place …

indicators.note: the old granny goes inside the word for a lodging-place

parts.note: a rest, as in rest house, is a place to lodge or stay
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly grandmother at a boarding house makes a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next only for the surface; the two have unconnected wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonant describes a sound that is deep, echoing and ringing.

clue.text: … on understanding that it's furnished

definitions.meaning: a conjunction meaning on condition that

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continuing from the previous clue is only for the surface; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Provided is both a conjunction meaning if or on condition that, and a past participle meaning supplied.

clue.text: Dominate the union, but shelter supporting members

definitions.meaning: to be the dominant partner in a marriage
literally, to cover the legs, the limbs that hold one up

explanation.walkthrough: 'members' means limbs here: the legs that support the body are what trousers cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being the boss in a household or marriage; read literally it is putting on leg coverings.

clue.text: Avoid offending relation

definitions.meaning: to show due regard for someone's wishes or rights
as in the phrase in this connection or reference

explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to avoid offending them; a respect is also a relation or reference, as in 'with respect to'.

clue.text: Long-serving surgeon managed to retain energy

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
E is the physics symbol for energy
ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: An animal doctor who still has plenty of energy after years in post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' puts E inside RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience in a job, a long-serving person.

clue.text: Preserves animals in part of vessel found in digs

definitions.text: part of vessel found in digs

parts.note: to pot food is to preserve it in a jar
a herd is a group of animals

explanation.surface: Jams and livestock among the household goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' means archaeological excavations, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a broken fragment of pottery, a common archaeological find.

clue.text: Archdeacon's about, say, for outside service

indicators.note: the letters for 'say' go round the rest

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven; the 's gives S
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A churchman wandering around outside during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' splits the letters for 'say' round the rest; 'for' is a link. An archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Tree with horse, possibly, going round it

indicators.note: the horse encircles the letter for 'with'

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat; 'possibly' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A tree with a horse circling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts W inside ROAN; 'it' simply refers back to W.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree with red berries.

clue.text: When it would be woeful to have another tot?

definitions.text: When it would be woeful to have another tot?

parts.words: When it would be woeful to have another tot?
parts.note: the old nursery rhyme says the child born on a certain weekday is full of woe, so giving birth then would be woeful

explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a drink but means a small child; the rhyme 'Monday's child' assigns woe to one day.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, the child born on this midweek day is full of woe.

clue.text: Easily carried and fit for drinking across river

indicators.note: the word for drinkable spans the river, holding it inside

parts.note: potable means safe to drink

explanation.surface: Light enough to carry and safe to drink on a river trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside POTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means light enough to be easily carried.

clue.text: Deck where the whole lot reportedly work?

indicators.note: the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: all means the whole lot
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Is there a deck on the ship where every hand labours?
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says ALL is heard as ORL, in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Stop parson entering enclosure on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed on top of the next
the clergyman goes into the enclosure

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
Rev, Reverend, is a parson's title

explanation.surface: Halt a vicar from getting into a field on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the enclosed piece comes before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening.

clue.text: Dole unexpectedly keeping woman in land of riches

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the woman inside
the letters of the word turn up in a surprise order

parts.note: Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Unemployment benefit unexpectedly maintains a woman in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' scrambles DOLE to ELDO, and 'keeping' opens it after EL to take in the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary city of gold, any place of fabulous wealth.

clue.text: Take back carrier climbing on front of truck

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed piece sits on top of the next
in a down clue the word goes upward, read in reverse

parts.note: a carter is someone who carries goods by cart

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Withdraw a haulier who climbed onto the truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns CARTER into RETRAC, set 'on' T.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back.

clue.text: In a word, where campers may be concentrated?

parts.note: campers sleep in a tent

explanation.surface: Where might campers be found clustered together?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a word' tells you to join IN and TENT into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent means concentrated or focused on something.

clue.text: Greek hero prosecutes over article used as leader

indicators.note: the article goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the word for prosecutes is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against

explanation.surface: A Greek hero taking someone to court over a newspaper leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SUES into SEUS; 'used as leader' puts THE first.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the hero of Greek myth who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Husband leaves woman in compound

indicators.note: the husband departs from the woman's name

parts.note: Hester is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A husband walks out on his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes H from HESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Difficult to accept new inhabitant of marsh

parts.note: a bitter pill is hard to swallow

explanation.surface: Hard to accept a newcomer to the wetlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like bird of reed beds and marshes.

clue.text: Leguminous shrub found in brush

definitions.meaning: a yellow-flowered plant of the pea family

explanation.definitionFit: Broom is both a shrub of the pea family and a sweeping brush.

clue.text: Don't tell, but the gatepost's gone The solution to Saturday's Prize missing!

annotationWithheld.why: clue as held is 'Don't tell, but the gatepost's gone The solution to Saturday's Prize missing!': a newspaper notice about a missing prize solution is spliced into the clue text
annotationWithheld.clue: Don't tell, but the gatepost's gone The solution to Saturday's Prize missing!

clue.text: List of corrections in Latin?

parts.note: a printed list of mistakes, whose name is a Latin plural meaning mistakes

explanation.walkthrough: The word is the Latin plural of erratum, an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An errata slip lists errors in a printed book with their corrections.

clue.text: Precious stone from boundaries of tiny Thames resort

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to sort them again into a new order
the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A gem found at a little riverside holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but means sort again: TY (first and last letters of 'tiny') and THAMES rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz used as a gemstone.
